memory_update.text: PDFS should be the primary direct underfollowed candidate for the semiconductor data/orchestration node; it maps most closely to cross-step manufacturing data harmonization, analytics, and AI/ML workflows.

Inspection and metrology vendors are second-order candidates for this node because they generate the measurement and defect data that feeds yield analytics and process-control systems, especially in HBM and advanced packaging.
CAMT is the strongest adjacent underfollowed equipment candidate in this pass because company materials directly reference advanced packaging, OSAT, memory, and recent HBM-related orders.

Need a separate validation pass on private or non-US-listed competitors in semiconductor MES, yield analytics, STDF/test-data analytics, and factory automation software to understand whether PDFS has a true chokepoint or only one public-market proxy.

node: Semiconductor manufacturing data, yield analytics, traceability, and orchestration software
summary: Expanded the universe around the semiconductor manufacturing data-orchestration node with a two-lane framing: PDF Solutions as the most direct underfollowed software/data orchestration candidate, and metrology/inspection vendors as second-order data-generation and yield-learning bottlenecks. The strongest direct fit is PDFS because its Exensio and related platforms explicitly target semiconductor manufacturing analytics, data harmonization, AI/ML workflows, and cross-step yield learning. CAMT, ONTO, and NVMI are not pure software-orchestration plays, but they are plausible adjacent chokepoint names because advanced packaging, HBM, chiplets, and heterogeneous integration require inspection/metrology data that feeds yield analytics and process control loops.
